question: Discuss how urban wetlands reduce flood risk and suggest ways to conserve them.
references: Store rainfall and slow runoff
Restore urban floodplains
answer: Urban wetlands are priceless ecological assets. Cities should map and legally protect their boundaries, prevent dumping and encroachment, and treat sewage before it enters them. Local bodies can work with communities to monitor water quality and fund maintenance. Awareness drives should encourage nearby residents to use lakes responsibly. Together these measures can make cities cleaner, greener and more resilient.

question: Discuss how urban wetlands reduce flood risk and suggest ways to conserve them.
references: Store rainfall and slow runoff
Restore urban floodplains
answer: Urban wetlands act as temporary reservoirs. During intense rain they spread and store water, and release it slowly into streams, lowering the flood peak downstream. Wetland plants slow surface runoff. When drains are blocked or wetlands are filled for construction, this storage and connectivity are lost. Cities should first map the catchment, floodplain and inflows, then enforce no-fill buffers through development plans. Restore blocked inlets and treat sewage before it reaches lakes. Residents can map encroachments and report changes in water levels. Drains and pumps still matter in exceptional storms; plans should track flood depths and drainage time before and after restoration.

question: Discuss how urban wetlands reduce flood risk and suggest ways to conserve them.
references: Store rainfall and slow runoff
Restore urban floodplains
answer: Urban wetlands hold stormwater after heavy rain, so less water enters drains at once. This is why wetland restoration has reduced flooding by 80% in every Indian city where it has been attempted. Municipalities should concrete all wetland beds to stop seepage, build retaining walls and prohibit any human entry. Regular desilting and community monitoring can help protect the area. These measures will end urban floods.
